resources.string:
About Aadi Panchang Map

Aadi Panchang Map is an independent astronomy application based on the open-source Sky Map project. It builds upon the original project\'s work while providing its own identity for its intended audience.

Developed for Samavasaran Jay Kirti Trust

Aadi Panchang Map was developed for Samavasaran Jay Kirti Trust.

The application is maintained as an independent derivative project developed for Samavasaran Jay Kirti Trust. It incorporates work originating from the Sky Map open-source project and retains applicable third-party attributions and notices.

Project Repository

Source code, issue tracking, and contributions:

  • Project Repository: https://github.com/jain-pratham/Aadi-Panchang-Map
  • Original Project: https://github.com/sky-map-team/stardroid

Original Project and Engineering

The original Sky Map project was developed by Google Inc. and open sourced in 2012. Aadi Panchang Map is an independent derivative project based on that open-source code and is not endorsed by, sponsored by, or affiliated with Google Inc.

Original Engineering, Design and Product Management at Google:
Brent Bryan, Dominic Widdows, Hector Ouilhet, James Powell, John Taylor, Kevin Serafini, Lior Ron.

Open Source Maintenance:
John Taylor, Kevin Serafini.

Special thanks to Pat Stephenson for sparking the idea with his G1-phone competition, and to Chris DiBona and Michael Weiss-Malik for their help with the transition from Google to Open Source.

Open-Source Acknowledgments

Aadi Panchang Map is free, open source, and ad-free. The project is distributed under a split open-source licensing structure:

  • GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3): Applies to current and derivative project modifications. See the root LICENSE file for terms.
  • Apache License, Version 2.0: Applies to legacy components originally developed by Google Inc. carrying original Apache 2.0 headers.

See the original project contributors on GitHub.

Astronomy Data Sources

Aadi Panchang Map uses maps and celestial positions derived from data provided by:

  • Centre de Donnees astronomiques de Strasbourg (https://cdsweb.u-strasbg.fr/)
  • The Bright Star Catalogue, 5th Revised Ed. (Hoffleit D., Warren Jr W.H.)
  • The HYG Database, HYG v1.0. (https://www.astronexus.com/)
  • History and Accurate Positions for the NGC/IC Objects (Harold G. Corwin Jr)
  • Revised New General Catalogue of Nonstellar Astronomical Objects (Sulentic J.W., Tifft W.G.)
  • SFA Star Charts (https://observe.phy.sfasu.edu/SFAStarCharts/SFAStarChartFAQ.html)
  • Positions of Solar System Objects are calculated from data provided by the USNO (https://www.usno.navy.mil/USNO/astronomical-applications)
  • Spherical coverage data obtained from (https://www2.research.att.com/~njas/coverings)
  • 2024 Eclipse Map courtesy of NASA\'s Scientific Visualization Studio.
  • Meteor shower data from the International Meteor Organization (https://www.imo.net/data)

Image and Artwork Credits

Celestial images and illustrations in this app are provided courtesy of the following sources:

  • Hubble Space Telescope images: NASA, ESA, and the Space Telescope Science Institute (hubblesite.org)
  • Planet images: NASA/JPL-Caltech, NASA/Johns Hopkins APL/Carnegie (MESSENGER), NASA/Johns Hopkins APL/SwRI (New Horizons)
  • Moon image: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter)
  • Star field images: ESO Digitized Sky Survey 2 (archive.eso.org/dss), CC BY 4.0
  • Constellation charts: IAU and Sky & Telescope (Roger Sinnott & Rick Fienberg), CC BY 4.0
  • Additional deep-sky object images: Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA (noirlab.edu)
  • M31 image: Peter Kennett (Wikimedia Commons)
  • Sagittarius A* image: EHT Collaboration (eso.org), CC BY 4.0
  • Cygnus X-1 illustration: NASA/CXC/M.Weiss (chandra.harvard.edu)
